writeup.headline: NetApp rates Buy on accelerating growth, strong margins and net cash, held back by a full valuation.
writeup.thesis: NetApp scores 71, a Buy, mainly on growth, quality, balance sheet and trend. Latest-quarter revenue growth of 29.9% year on year (growth sped up by 17.4 pp from the previous quarter) and TTM revenue growth of 12.2% give a growth score of 82. Quality also scores 82, with a 70.6% gross margin, 25.0% operating margin, 22.3% FCF margin and the diluted share count down 1.5% year on year. The balance sheet holds net cash and scores 95, and the shares show strong momentum, up 80.8% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and 97.9 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation is the drag at 29: multiples are high in absolute terms (5.9x sales, 26.6x FCF, 23.2x EV/EBIT, FCF yield 1.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), and the stock is expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends on all three multiples.
key_risks: Valuation is expensive against its own history and high in absolute terms, leaving little room for a growth disappointment.
The sharp run-up (price 50.1% above its 200-day average) could reverse if AI storage enthusiasm cools.
Insiders sold with no buying, including open-market sales by two directors.
Barclays downgraded on valuation, a sign some analysts see the price as full.
The latest-quarter growth spike may not persist at that pace.
what_would_change: A drop of more than 7 points in the score, for example from weaker news or slowing growth, would move the rating to Hold.
A gain of 9 points would reach Strong Buy, most plausibly through a better valuation score if the price eased while earnings kept growing.
A break in momentum would pull down the trend score of 96, which currently props up the rating.
Further insider selling or analyst downgrades would weigh on the news risk score of 56.
